requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'Chip Placement with Deep Reinforcement Learning' have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The compute environment, EDA tooling access, and supporting libraries required to run the placement pipeline are available.
The Python environment and deep learning framework required to build and train the policy/value networks are installed and configured.

Code has been implemented to specify Python version (>=3.6) and install a deep learning framework (e.g., TensorFlow or PyTorch) capable of expressing graph neural network operations, deconvolutional layers, and PPO training.

verification.spec: Run `python --version` and assert version >= 3.6. Then attempt `import tensorflow` or `import torch` and confirm one succeeds; verify the chosen framework can define a Conv2DTranspose/deconvolution layer, a simple message-passing GNN op, and a basic PPO-style clipped objective in a smoke test.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to install numerical and scientific Python libraries (numpy, scipy) as well as a graph processing library sufficient to represent netlists as adjacency structures.

verification.spec: Run `python -c 'import numpy, scipy, networkx'` (or equivalent graph library such as igraph) and assert all imports succeed with printable versions. Confirm a netlist can be represented as an adjacency structure via a small smoke test.

sub_tasks.requirements: A dependency manifest (e.g., requirements.txt or environment.yml) is provided that pins all libraries needed to reproduce the training pipeline end-to-end.

verification.spec: Check that a requirements.txt or environment.yml file exists at the repository root, that every listed dependency has a pinned version (== or exact tag), and that `pip install -r requirements.txt` (or `conda env create -f environment.yml`) into a fresh virtualenv succeeds and imports all top-level modules used by the training entrypoint.

sub_tasks.requirements: Hardware acceleration and distributed training infrastructure for PPO with many parallel rollouts are available.
Code has been implemented to detect and utilize at least one GPU (or TPU) for training the policy/value networks, with fallback to CPU for smaller inference runs.

verification.spec: Run the training entrypoint on a machine with a visible NVIDIA GPU; confirm via logs (or torch.cuda.is_available() / tf.config.list_physical_devices('GPU')) that the model is placed on GPU. Then set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' and rerun a short inference smoke test; confirm it falls back to CPU without error.

sub_tasks.requirements: External EDA tooling and netlist-processing utilities required by the placement pipeline are accessible.

The hMETIS hypergraph partitioner (Karypis & Kumar, 1998) is installed and callable from the pipeline to cluster millions of standard cells into a few thousand clusters prior to force-directed placement.

verification.spec: Run `which shmetis` (or `khmetis`) and confirm the hMETIS binary is on PATH. Then invoke it on a small hypergraph file with a known partition count and assert (a) exit code 0, (b) an output partition file is produced with the requested number of partitions.

sub_tasks.requirements: The RePlAce baseline binary (Cheng et al., 2019) is installed and invocable with configurable optimization goals for the Table 2 comparison.

verification.spec: Locate the RePlAce executable, invoke it with `--help` and assert exit code 0. Then run RePlAce on a small provided benchmark (e.g., ISPD or a bundled toy netlist) and assert that it produces an output placement file with legal macro coordinates.

sub_tasks.requirements: The chip-placement RL environment is exposed via a standard interface with efficient reward computation.

The environment's reward computation (HPWL + congestion evaluation for one full placement) executes on the order of milliseconds per query, enabling the 100,000s of evaluations required to train PPO within the reported wall-clock budget.

verification.spec: Within the RL training environment, call env.step(...) on the terminal action (which triggers force-directed standard cell placement and reward calculation) for a representative block; measure end-to-end wall-clock latency averaged over 100 iterations. Assert mean latency is on the order of tens of ms (allowing up to ~50 ms).

sub_tasks.requirements: Experiment orchestration, logging, and checkpointing infrastructure is in place.
Code has been implemented to periodically checkpoint policy/value network weights so that pre-trained weights can later be loaded for zero-shot inference and finetuning on unseen blocks.

verification.spec: Run training for a short duration (e.g., 3 iterations) with checkpointing enabled at a small interval. Assert (a) checkpoint files are written to the expected directory with monotonically increasing step numbers, (b) a fresh process can load the latest checkpoint into a freshly instantiated policy/value network and reproduce (bit-exact or near-exact) the pre-checkpoint output on a fixed input.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to log per-iteration training metrics (reward, wirelength, congestion, PPO loss) and wall-clock time so that convergence plots (Figure 4) and dataset-size comparisons (Figure 5) can be reproduced.

verification.spec: Run training for a short duration (e.g., 5 iterations). Assert that a structured log (TensorBoard event file, CSV, or JSONL) is produced containing per-iteration entries for reward, wirelength, congestion, PPO loss, and wall-clock timestamp. Parse the log and verify all five fields are populated and monotonic timestamps advance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The TPU chip block netlists (or suitable proxies) and the 10,000-placement supervised dataset have been prepared, along with hMETIS-based standard cell clustering and grid discretization.
Netlist inputs (TPU accelerator blocks or open-source proxies) are acquired and parsed into the graph representation used by the placer.

Code has been implemented to acquire and load a set of chip netlists (either the proprietary TPU blocks or public proxies such as Ariane RISC-V), including at least 5 distinct blocks for the supervised dataset and 20+ blocks for the largest training set experiment in Section 5.2.

verification.spec: Run the data-loading script and assert that (a) at least 5 distinct netlists are available for building the supervised dataset (each parseable into a graph), (b) a larger training set of at least 20 blocks is available for the largest experiment. Print a summary table (block_name, num_macros, num_std_cells) verifying diversity.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to parse each netlist into a graph structure with macros, standard cells, and nets as edges/hyperedges, exposing node types (macro/std-cell), widths, heights, and connectivity.

verification.spec: Load a sample netlist file and call the parser. Assert the returned object exposes: node list with per-node fields (type in {macro, std_cell}, width, height), edge/hyperedge list encoding nets, and a query API for adjacency. Cross-check node/edge counts against ground-truth values from the source file header.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to extract per-netlist metadata (horizontal/vertical routing capacity, total number of nets, macros, standard cell clusters, canvas width/height, number of rows/columns) required as inputs to the metadata embedding network.

verification.spec: For a sample netlist, call the metadata extractor and assert the returned dict includes fields: horizontal_routing_capacity, vertical_routing_capacity, num_nets, num_macros, num_std_cell_clusters, canvas_width, canvas_height, num_rows, num_cols. Verify each value is a positive scalar and dimensions are consistent (e.g., num_rows*num_cols <= 128*128).

sub_tasks.requirements: The prepared test set includes 5 unseen target blocks (Blocks 1-5) with a variety of block types (memory subsystems, compute units, and control logic), each with up to a few hundred macros and millions of standard cells.

verification.spec: Enumerate the 5 configured test blocks and assert (a) count == 5, (b) each block has num_macros between roughly 10 and 1000 (up to a few hundred), (c) each has num_std_cells on the order of >= 100k (millions target), (d) block types cover at least 2 of {memory, compute, control} (verifiable via a labels field or naming convention).

sub_tasks.requirements: Standard cells are clustered with hMETIS into a few thousand clusters using the normalized minimum cut objective.

Code has been implemented to invoke hMETIS (Karypis & Kumar, 1998) on the netlist hypergraph to partition standard cells into a configurable number of clusters (a few thousand) using the normalized minimum cut objective.

verification.spec: Invoke the clustering wrapper on a small synthetic hypergraph (e.g., 1000 nodes) requesting k clusters (e.g., 50). Verify hMETIS (or its Python binding) is called, that the returned partition assigns each node to a cluster id in [0, k), and that the number of clusters matches the requested value.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to remap the original netlist edges onto the clustered nodes, aggregating connections between clusters so that force-directed placement and reward computation operate on the reduced (macro + cluster) graph.

verification.spec: Build a small synthetic netlist with N original std cells partitioned into K known clusters. Run the edge remapping and assert (a) each remapped edge references only cluster ids (0..K-1) or macro ids, (b) for each original edge between std cells in clusters A and B, a corresponding cluster-level edge (A,B) exists in the remapped graph, (c) the total number of cluster-level edges is <= the total number of original edges (aggregation preserved).

sub_tasks.requirements: Given a netlist with millions of standard cells, hMETIS clustering produces on the order of a few thousand clusters (verifiable as being in the low-thousands range, not tens of thousands or hundreds).

verification.spec: Instantiate the hMETIS-based clustering step on a representative netlist containing on the order of millions of standard cells (or a synthetic hypergraph of similar scale). Count the resulting number of clusters and assert it falls in the low-thousands range (i.e., ~3000, order of magnitude 10^3).

sub_tasks.requirements: The chip canvas is discretized into a grid with row/column selection driven by bin-packing over wasted space.
Code has been implemented to discretize the 2D chip canvas into an m x n grid and snap the center of each macro or standard cell cluster to the center of its assigned grid cell.

verification.spec: Instantiate the canvas discretizer with a chosen m and n and a canvas width/height. Place several macros/clusters at arbitrary continuous coordinates and call the snap function. Assert (a) each returned coordinate is exactly the center of some grid cell (i.e., ((i+0.5)*width/m, (j+0.5)*height/n)), (b) the chosen cell (i,j) is the one whose center is closest to the input coordinate.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to select the number of rows and columns by ranking combinations according to wasted space (a bin-packing formulation) and choosing the best trade-off, with the maximum limited to 128 rows and 128 columns.

verification.spec: Call the row/column selector with a canvas of known dimensions and a set of macro sizes. Assert (a) returned rows <= 128 and cols <= 128, (b) the chosen (rows, cols) minimizes a wasted-space objective compared to a brute-force search over all combinations (1..128, 1..128) for a small test case, (c) selector rejects any candidate that exceeds 128 in either dimension.

sub_tasks.requirements: Across the evaluated blocks, the row/column selection procedure produces an average of approximately 30 rows and 30 columns as reported in Section 3.3.2.

verification.spec: Run the row/column selection (bin-packing) procedure on each of the evaluated blocks with the paper's constraint of max 128 rows/columns. Record chosen rows and columns per block; compute the mean of (rows + columns)/2 across blocks. Assert the mean is approximately 30.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to pad any grid smaller than 128x128 by masking the unused L-shaped region so that all inputs to the policy network share a canonical 128x128 grid size.

verification.spec: Instantiate the policy input pipeline with grid sizes smaller than 128x128 (e.g., 30x30, 64x100). Verify the returned tensor has shape 128x128 and that positions outside the actual grid are masked (mask value True/1 for L-shaped unused region). Check that the masked action logits are set to -inf or excluded from argmax so the policy cannot place there.

sub_tasks.requirements: The 10,000-placement supervised dataset with wirelength and congestion labels has been constructed from 5 accelerator netlists.
Code has been implemented to select 5 different accelerator netlists as the source netlists for the supervised placement-quality dataset.

verification.spec: Inspect the dataset generation script/config and confirm it selects exactly 5 distinct accelerator netlists as source netlists for the supervised placement-quality dataset (per Section 4.1, '5 different accelerator netlists'). Verify programmatically by loading the dataset manifest and counting unique netlist identifiers.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to generate 2,000 placements per source netlist, yielding a total of 10,000 (placement, netlist) pairs.

verification.spec: Locate the dataset-generation script/module. Verify via code inspection and/or a dry run that it iterates over exactly 5 source netlists and produces 2,000 placements each, yielding 10,000 (placement, reward) pairs total. Confirm the output file/dir contains 10,000 records.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each dataset example is labeled with its computed proxy wirelength and proxy congestion values, matching the reward-function definitions, and is stored alongside the state features (adjacency, node features, current macro id, metadata).

verification.spec: Load a sample of dataset examples and verify each contains: state features (adjacency matrix, node features, current macro id, metadata) and labels (proxy wirelength, proxy congestion). Recompute the labels from the stored state features using the reward-function code and confirm they match the stored labels within numerical tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The dataset is split for training and held-out evaluation of the supervised reward-prediction model in a manner that allows measuring generalization to unseen netlists.

verification.spec: Inspect the dataset split logic and confirm it partitions examples such that at least one netlist is held out entirely (no placements of a test netlist appear in training). Load the train and eval splits and verify the sets of netlist identifiers are disjoint.

sub_tasks.requirements: Training-set-size scaling data splits (2, 5, and 20 TPU blocks) are prepared as nested subsets.

Code has been implemented to construct three pre-training datasets containing 2, 5, and 20 TPU blocks respectively, where the smaller sets are strict subsets of the larger ones as described in Section 5.2.

verification.spec: Load the three declared pre-training dataset manifests. Assert they contain exactly 2, 5, and 20 TPU block identifiers respectively; assert the 2-block set is a subset of the 5-block set, and the 5-block set is a subset of the 20-block set.

sub_tasks.requirements: The dataset composition covers a variety of block types (memory subsystems, compute units, and control logic) as described in Section 5.2.

verification.spec: Load the dataset manifest and confirm the block metadata tags each block with a type. Verify that the training set contains at least one block of each category: memory subsystem, compute unit, and control logic (per Section 5.2).

sub_tasks.requirements: The proxy reward function combining half-perimeter wirelength, routing congestion (with 5x1 smoothing and top-10% averaging), and the density hard constraint has been implemented as specified in Section 3.3.
The half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL) proxy cost is implemented per Section 3.3.1 (Equations 1-2).
Code has been implemented that computes per-net HPWL as the half-perimeter of the bounding box of all pins/nodes connected to that net (max(x) - min(x) + max(y) - min(y)).

verification.spec: Import the HPWL function; construct several small nets with known pin (x,y) coordinates (e.g., 2-pin, 3-pin, and 5-pin nets); verify the returned value equals (max(x)-min(x)) + (max(y)-min(y)) for each. Include edge cases: single-pin net (returns 0) and collinear pins.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that aggregates HPWL across nets by applying the per-net normalization factor q(i) and summing over all nets in the netlist as in Equation 2.

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic netlist with several nets of varying pin counts; compute expected total HPWL by manually applying per-net q(i) normalization and summing over N_netlist. Assert the module's aggregate HPWL matches this expected value, and that changing q(i) changes the output as expected.

sub_tasks.requirements: Wires leaving a standard-cell cluster are treated as originating at the center of the cluster (per the reward approximation in Section 3.3), and macros/clusters are placed at grid-cell centers when computing HPWL.

verification.spec: Construct a small synthetic netlist with known cluster/macro positions. Invoke the HPWL computation and verify that (a) the pin positions for standard-cell clusters used in bounding-box computation equal the cluster center coordinate, and (b) macro and cluster positions are snapped to the corresponding grid-cell center coordinates before HPWL is computed.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a small synthetic netlist with known pin coordinates, the implemented HPWL function returns the analytically expected value (deterministic unit-behavior check).

verification.spec: Create a synthetic netlist with fully specified pin coordinates whose HPWL can be computed by hand (e.g., 4 nets with known bounding boxes). Assert the HPWL implementation returns the exact analytical values (within floating-point tolerance).

sub_tasks.requirements: Proxy routing congestion is computed as described in Section 3.3.5, including deterministic routing, separate H/V tracking, 5x1 smoothing, and top-10% averaging.
Code has been implemented that performs simple deterministic net routing based on driver and load pin locations, allocating routing resources to each grid cell the route passes through.

verification.spec: Create a small synthetic net with a driver and two loads at known grid positions. Call the deterministic routing function and verify: (a) the returned route occupies grid cells along a deterministic path between driver and loads (e.g., L-shape or Steiner-like), (b) the same call twice produces the same route (deterministic), and (c) resource usage is incremented on each traversed grid cell.

sub_tasks.requirements: Vertical and horizontal routing usage per grid cell are tracked in separate arrays, and each cell's available capacity is derived from a configurable per-technology routing-resource parameter.

verification.spec: Instantiate the congestion tracker with a configurable per-cell horizontal and vertical routing-resource parameter. Route a horizontal-only net; verify horizontal usage increases while vertical usage remains unchanged. Route a vertical-only net; verify the reverse. Confirm the resource values come from a technology config parameter, not hardcoded.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies a 5x1 convolutional smoothing filter to both the vertical and horizontal congestion maps in their respective directions.

verification.spec: Construct a small random horizontal and vertical congestion map; apply the smoothing filter and verify it corresponds to a 5x1 convolution applied along the horizontal axis (for horizontal map) and along the vertical axis (for vertical map). Compare against manual convolution result on interior cells.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a small hand-computed congestion map, the 5x1 smoothing implementation returns the expected values at both interior and boundary cells (unit behavior check).

verification.spec: Construct a small congestion grid (e.g., 8x8) with hand-set values; hand-compute the 5x1 filtered output at both interior locations and boundary locations (using whatever padding scheme the implementation declares). Assert the smoothing implementation matches these hand-computed values exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: The congestion cost is computed as the average of the top 10% most congested grid cells (ABA10-style) over the combined smoothed congestion values across the canvas.

verification.spec: Given a smoothed congestion grid, verify the congestion cost returned equals the mean of the top 10% highest values across the combined horizontal+vertical values on the canvas. Test with a small grid where the top 10% can be identified by inspection.

sub_tasks.requirements: On a controlled test grid where 10% of the cells have known values, the top-10% averaging implementation returns exactly the mean of those values (unit behavior check).

verification.spec: Build a controlled grid of size N where 10% of cells have value V and the rest are 0; assert top-10% average routine returns exactly V. Then set 10% of cells to distinct known values v1..vk and verify the result equals their arithmetic mean.

sub_tasks.requirements: Density is enforced as a hard constraint via a binary density mask (Section 3.3.6).

Code has been implemented that constructs an m x n binary density mask at each RL step, marking grid cells where placing the center of the current macro would keep every affected grid cell's occupied area at or below max_density.

verification.spec: Create a synthetic partial placement on an m x n grid with several placed macros and a current macro of known w x h; call the density mask function with max_density=0.6. Verify the mask is m x n binary and that a cell is marked 1 iff placing the current macro's center there keeps every overlapped grid cell's occupied area <= 0.6.

sub_tasks.requirements: The max_density threshold is configurable and defaults to 0.6 as used in the paper's experiments.

verification.spec: Inspect the code/config: confirm a `max_density` (or equivalent) parameter is exposed on the environment/config object, that it defaults to 0.6, and that changing it changes the density-mask threshold. E.g., assert env.max_density == 0.6 by default, and that env(max_density=0.4).max_density == 0.4.

sub_tasks.requirements: The density mask additionally forbids cells whose occupation would create infeasible macro overlap with previously placed macros, and marks blocked/blockage regions (e.g., clock straps) as density 1 so no macro can be placed there.

verification.spec: Construct a canvas with (a) one already-placed macro and (b) a defined blockage region. Call the density-mask update for a new macro of known size and verify: (i) all cells overlapping the placed macro's footprint are masked (infeasible), (ii) all cells in the blockage region have density set to 1 and are masked. Compare against manually computed expected mask.

sub_tasks.requirements: Action selection takes the element-wise product of the density mask and the policy network's output distribution over the grid and then selects the argmax (or samples) over feasible locations only, preventing infeasible placements.

verification.spec: Set up a policy forward pass returning a known logits/probability grid, and provide a density mask with several infeasible cells. Call the action-selection function and verify: (a) infeasible cells are set to 0 probability (or -inf logit) via element-wise product/masking, (b) the returned argmax is a feasible cell even when the raw argmax would fall on an infeasible one.

sub_tasks.requirements: On a synthetic canvas with a partially placed macro of known size and a max_density of 0.6, the density mask marks exactly the analytically expected set of infeasible cells (unit behavior check).

verification.spec: On a 10x10 canvas with one pre-placed macro occupying known cells and a current macro of known dimensions, hand-compute the set of grid cells where placing the current macro's center would keep every affected cell <= 0.6 occupancy. Assert the density mask matches this set exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: The overall proxy reward combines wirelength and congestion under the density hard constraint per Equation 4.

Code has been implemented that returns reward 0 at every intermediate step t < T and, at t = T, returns the negative weighted sum -(Wirelength(p,g) + lambda * Congestion(p,g)) subject to density(p,g) <= max_density.

verification.spec: Run a simulated episode with T macros; step the environment and assert r_t == 0 for all t < T. At t = T (all macros placed and standard cells FD-placed), assert reward equals -(wirelength + lambda*congestion) with the same wirelength and congestion computed independently, and that placements violating density return a masked/penalized reward as specified.

sub_tasks.requirements: The congestion weight lambda is a configurable hyperparameter, defaulting to 0.01 as used in the paper's experiments.

verification.spec: Inspect the reward/config code: confirm a `congestion_weight` (lambda) parameter is exposed, defaults to 0.01, and is actually used in the weighted reward combination R = -(WL + lambda*congestion). Assert config.congestion_weight == 0.01 by default and that overriding it changes reward output.

sub_tasks.requirements: The full proxy reward function evaluates in on the order of a few milliseconds per placement on a single CPU thread for a representative test netlist, satisfying the paper's speed requirement for use inside the RL loop.

verification.spec: Load a representative test netlist. Time the full proxy reward function (wirelength + congestion on a completed macro+cluster placement) over 1000 invocations on a single CPU thread. Report the mean per-call latency in milliseconds; assert it is on the order of a few milliseconds (single-digit to low double-digit ms).

sub_tasks.requirements: For placements that violate the density constraint (i.e., no feasible action for some macro), the reward pipeline treats them as invalid rather than returning a finite score, consistent with the hard-constraint formulation.

verification.spec: Construct a scenario where placement of a mid-sequence macro is infeasible (density mask entirely masked). Call the environment step function and verify the episode returns an invalid/failure signal (e.g., raises, returns a done=True with a distinct invalid flag, or returns None/NaN reward) rather than a finite proxy cost.

sub_tasks.requirements: Correlation and postprocessing behaviors of the proxy reward are validated as described in Section 3.3 and 3.3.7.

On a set of placements of a single block, the proxy HPWL is measured to be positively correlated (Pearson r > 0) with the commercial-EDA-tool total wirelength reported for those placements, as required for the proxy to be a useful reward signal.

verification.spec: Generate 20+ placements of the same block (varying seed or policy checkpoint). For each, compute proxy HPWL and obtain total wirelength from the commercial EDA tool (or from a mocked ground-truth wirelength surrogate if EDA unavailable). Compute Pearson correlation r between the two arrays across placements. Assert r > 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, after RL placement of macros, performs a greedy legalization step snapping macros to the nearest legal position while honoring minimum spacing constraints before EDA-tool evaluation (Section 3.3.7).

verification.spec: Provide a placement with slightly overlapping macros or macros whose positions violate the min-spacing rule. Invoke the greedy legalizer and verify (a) each macro is moved to the nearest legal position, (b) resulting placement contains no overlaps and satisfies min-spacing, (c) the total displacement is small (greedy nearest-legal, not global re-place).

sub_tasks.requirements: The graph neural network encoder that produces node/edge embeddings via the update equations in Section 4.1, along with the supervised regression task to predict wirelength and congestion, has been implemented and trained.
The GNN encoder that ingests netlist adjacency and per-node features and produces node and edge embeddings via the iterative message-passing updates of Equation 5 is implemented.

Node input features (node type, width, height, x-coordinate, y-coordinate) are constructed for each macro and standard cell cluster and concatenated to form the initial per-node feature vector fed to the encoder.

verification.spec: Load a small netlist and call the feature construction function. For each macro and standard-cell cluster, verify the initial feature vector concatenates exactly: node type (categorical/one-hot), width, height, x-coordinate, y-coordinate. Confirm the feature vector length and per-index semantics via direct inspection on 3 sample nodes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Node embeddings v_i and edge embeddings e_ij are randomly initialized as 32-dimensional vectors for all nodes and edges of the netlist graph.

verification.spec: Inspect the graph-neural-network module initialization code: assert node embedding tensors and edge embedding tensors are created with last dimension = 32 and are initialized with a random (non-constant) initializer for every node and edge in the netlist.

sub_tasks.requirements: The edge update step computes e_ij = fc_1( concat(v_i, v_j) * w^e_ij ) using a 65x32 feedforward network fc_1 with per-edge learnable scalar weights w^e_ij.

verification.spec: Inspect the edge-update module: verify fc_1 is a feedforward network with input dim 65 and output dim 32; verify there is a learnable per-edge scalar weight w^e_ij; verify the forward pass concatenates v_i and v_j (32+32=64, plus 1 for edge weight => 65) and applies fc_1 to produce the 32-d edge embedding.

sub_tasks.requirements: The node update step sets v_i to the mean of the embeddings of edges incident on v_i (aggregated over N(v_i)) with fc_0 (32x32) applied appropriately per Equation 5.

verification.spec: Inspect the node-update module: verify fc_0 is a 32->32 feedforward and that node v_i is updated by taking the mean of embeddings of edges incident on v_i (over N(v_i)). Run a forward pass on a small hand-constructed graph and confirm the update matches Equation 5.

sub_tasks.requirements: The GNN performs multiple iterations of alternating edge and node updates, producing final node and edge embeddings that are returned as outputs of the encoder.

verification.spec: Instantiate the GNN encoder with a configurable number of message-passing rounds (>=2). Run a forward pass on a small netlist and verify: (a) node and edge embeddings are updated across rounds (embedding at round k differs from round k-1 by more than a numerical epsilon), (b) the encoder returns both final node embeddings and final edge embeddings as outputs (not just one).

sub_tasks.requirements: A graph-level netlist embedding is produced by applying a reduce-mean function over all final edge embeddings.

verification.spec: Instantiate the GNN encoder, run a forward pass on a small synthetic netlist, and verify that the returned graph-level embedding equals the elementwise mean of the final edge embedding tensor along the edge axis (i.e., torch.allclose(graph_emb, edge_embs.mean(dim=edge_axis))).

sub_tasks.requirements: The current-macro node embedding is exposed as a separate output of the encoder (indexed by the id of the macro currently being placed) so downstream policy/value heads can consume it.

verification.spec: Call the encoder with a batch of synthetic netlists and a current_macro_id argument; assert that a separate 'current_node_embedding' output is returned with shape [batch, 32] and that its value equals the node embedding tensor indexed at current_macro_id.

sub_tasks.requirements: The supervised regression model that predicts wirelength and congestion from a placement state is built by combining the GNN encoder with a metadata embedding branch and a prediction head.

A feedforward metadata embedding network encodes horizontal and vertical routing capacity, total number of nets, number of macros, number of standard cell clusters, canvas size, and number of grid rows and columns.

verification.spec: Import the metadata embedding module and verify it is a feedforward network accepting a feature vector containing horizontal routing capacity, vertical routing capacity, number of nets, number of macros, number of standard cell clusters, canvas width, canvas height, num_rows, num_cols. Confirm via a forward pass with a dummy metadata tensor that an embedding vector is produced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The prediction head is a fully connected feedforward network whose input is the concatenation of the graph (reduce-mean edge) embedding and the metadata embedding and whose output is a reward prediction (wirelength and congestion).

verification.spec: Construct the supervised reward-prediction model, provide dummy graph+metadata inputs, and verify: (a) the prediction head takes as input the concatenation of the reduce-mean edge embedding and the metadata embedding, (b) the head is a feedforward network, (c) it outputs two scalars (wirelength and congestion predictions).

sub_tasks.requirements: The supervised loss is the weighted sum of the mean squared error on wirelength and the mean squared error on congestion targets.

verification.spec: Call the loss function with predictions and targets for wirelength and congestion; verify that the returned loss equals w1*MSE(wl_pred, wl_target) + w2*MSE(cong_pred, cong_target) for the configured weights (test with hand-computed values on tiny tensors).

sub_tasks.requirements: Grid-size handling sets the internal grid to 128x128 and masks the unused L-shaped region for netlists with fewer than 128 rows/columns, both during supervised training and downstream use.

verification.spec: Construct netlists with grid sizes such as (20, 20), (64, 100), (128, 128); run the model forward. Assert that internal action logits tensor is 128x128 and that positions outside the specified row/column extent (the L-shaped region) are masked to -inf or 0 probability after masking.

sub_tasks.requirements: The supervised training pipeline consumes the 10,000-placement dataset, trains the regression model, and produces a checkpoint reusable as the policy/value encoder.
A training loop performs regression on (state, wirelength, congestion) tuples using minibatch stochastic gradient optimization until validation loss plateaus.

verification.spec: Run the supervised training script on a tiny dataset of (state, wirelength, congestion) tuples for a few epochs and verify: (a) training performs minibatch SGD-style updates (loss decreases over iterations), (b) a validation-based early-stopping / plateau condition halts training when validation loss stops improving.
